For example if the interest rate is 5% per year and the amount will be received in three years the present value is the future amount divided by 1.05 cubed. The result tells us how much should be invested today at the same rate to grow to the promised amount. Any change in the rate or the time horizon will change the discount factor and therefore the present value.
